sanskrit: tathā hi musalair hanyuḥ śarīraṃ tat punar bhavet pṛthag jñānaṃ yad anyac ca yenaitan nopalabhyate
english: For though one should batter this body with clubs, it would arise again; and the knowing self is distinct, something other—that by which this body is not apprehended.

sanskrit: ṛtuḥ saṃvatsaras tithyaḥ śītoṣṇe ca priyāpriye yathātītāni paśyanti tādṛśaḥ sattvasaṃkṣayaḥ
english: As men behold the season, the year, the lunar days, cold and heat, the pleasant and the unpleasant, all as things gone by—of such a kind is the dissolution of a living being.

sanskrit: jarayā hi parītasya mṛtyunā vā vināśinā durbalaṃ durbalaṃ pūrvaṃ gṛhasyeva vinaśyati
english: For when one is beset by old age or by perishing death, what is weakest perishes first, just as the weakest part of a house gives way before the rest.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi mano vāyuḥ śoṇitaṃ māṃsam asthi ca ānupūrvyā vinaśyanti svaṃ dhātum upayānti ca
english: The senses, the mind, the breath, the blood, the flesh, and the bone perish each in its order and return into their own elements.

sanskrit: lokayātrāvidhānaṃ ca dānadharmaphalāgamaḥ yadarthaṃ vedaśabdāś ca vyavahārāś ca laukikāḥ
english: The ordering of the world's affairs, the coming of the fruits of giving and of duty, the very purpose for which the words of the Veda exist, and the customs of common life—

sanskrit: iti samyaṅ manasy ete bahavaḥ santi hetavaḥ etad astīdam astīti na kiṃ cit pratipadyate
english: thus, when rightly weighed in the mind, these many grounds for doubt are present; and saying 'this exists, that exists,' one arrives at no certainty at all.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vimṛśatām evaṃ tat tat samabhidhāvatām kva cin niviśate buddhis tatra jīryati vṛkṣavat
english: For those who ponder thus, running after this conclusion and that, the understanding settles somewhere at last, and there it grows old like a rooted tree.

sanskrit: evam arthair anarthaiś ca duḥkhitāḥ sarvajantavaḥ āgamair apakṛṣyante hastipair hastino yathā
english: Thus all creatures, made wretched by gains and by losses, are dragged about by the scriptures as elephants are dragged about by their drivers.

sanskrit: arthāṃs tathātyantasukhāvahāṃś ca; lipsanta ete bahavo viśulkāḥ mahattaraṃ duḥkham abhiprapannā; hitvāmiṣaṃ mṛtyuvaśaṃ prayānti
english: Coveting riches and the things that bring boundless pleasure, these many men squander all and, falling into a still greater misery, let go the bait and pass into the power of death.

sanskrit: vināśino hy adhruvajīvitasya; kiṃ bandhubhir mitraparigrahaiś ca vihāya yo gacchati sarvam eva; kṣaṇena gatvā na nivartate ca
english: For one who perishes, whose life is unstable, what use are kinsmen and the keeping of friends?—for he who departs leaves all behind, and once gone in an instant, returns no more.

sanskrit: bhūvyomatoyānalavāyavo hi; sadā śarīraṃ paripālayanti itīdam ālakṣya kuto ratir bhaved; vināśino hy asya na śarma vidyate
english: For earth, ether, water, fire, and wind forever sustain the body; perceiving this, whence should delight arise?—for one who is perishable, no lasting refuge is to be found.

sanskrit: idam anupadhi vākyam acchalaṃ; paramanirāmayam ātmasākṣikam narapatir abhivīkṣya vismitaḥ; punar anuyoktum idaṃ pracakrame
english: Beholding this speech, free of guile, without deceit, supremely sound, attested by the self, the king was amazed, and set himself once more to inquire thus.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca janako janadevas tu jñāpitaḥ paramarṣiṇā punar evānupapraccha sāṃparāye bhavābhavau
english: Bhīṣma said: But Janaka, lord of his people, having been instructed by the supreme sage, inquired yet again concerning being and non-being in the world beyond.

sanskrit: bhagavan yad idaṃ pretya saṃjñā bhavati kasya cit evaṃ sati kim ajñānaṃ jñānaṃ vā kiṃ kariṣyati
english: Reverend one, if it be that after death some consciousness arises for someone, then in that case what will ignorance avail, or what will knowledge accomplish?

sanskrit: sarvam ucchedaniṣṭhaṃ syāt paśya caitad dvijottama apramattaḥ pramatto vā kiṃ viśeṣaṃ kariṣyati
english: All would end in annihilation—consider this too, O best of the twice-born: what difference will it make whether a man be heedful or heedless?

sanskrit: asaṃsargo hi bhūteṣu saṃsargo vā vināśiṣu kasmai kriyeta kalpena niścayaḥ ko 'tra tattvataḥ
english: For if there is no contact among the elements, or contact only among perishable things, for whose sake should one strive after a rule? What here is certain in truth?

sanskrit: tamasā hi praticchannaṃ vibhrāntam iva cāturam punaḥ praśamayan vākyaiḥ kaviḥ pañcaśikho 'bravīt
english: To him, veiled in darkness, bewildered as it were, and distressed, the sage Pañcaśikha, calming him once more with his words, spoke.

sanskrit: ucchedaniṣṭhā nehāsti bhāvaniṣṭhā na vidyate ayaṃ hy api samāhāraḥ śarīrendriyacetasām vartate pṛthag anyonyam apy apāśritya karmasu
english: There is here no ending in annihilation, nor is there any abiding in fixed existence; for this aggregate too—of body, senses, and mind—operates, each part resting upon the other in their several works.

sanskrit: dhātavaḥ pañcaśākho 'yaṃ khaṃ vāyur jyotir ambu bhūḥ te svabhāvena tiṣṭhanti viyujyante svabhāvataḥ
english: The elements are this fivefold branching—ether, wind, fire, water, earth; by their own nature they hold together, and by their own nature they fall apart.

sanskrit: ākāśaṃ vāyur ūṣmā ca sneho yac cāpi pārthivam eṣa pañcasamāhāraḥ śarīram iti naikadhā jñānam ūṣmā ca vāyuś ca trividhaḥ karmasaṃgrahaḥ
english: Ether, wind, heat, moisture, and whatever is earthen—this fivefold gathering is called the body, manifold in nature; knowledge, heat, and wind make up the threefold sum of action.

sanskrit: indriyāṇīndriyārthāś ca svabhāvaś cetanā manaḥ prāṇāpānau vikāraś ca dhātavaś cātra niḥsṛtāḥ
english: The senses and their objects, the inherent nature, consciousness, the mind, the outbreath and inbreath, the modifications, and the elements—all these issue forth here.

sanskrit: śravaṇaṃ sparśanaṃ jihvā dṛṣṭir nāsā tathaiva ca indriyāṇīti pañcaite cittapūrvaṃgamā guṇāḥ
english: Hearing, touch, the tongue, sight, and the nose as well—these five are called the senses, qualities led on by the mind.

sanskrit: tatra vijñānasaṃyuktā trividhā vedanā dhruvā sukhaduḥkheti yām āhur aduḥkhety asukheti ca
english: Therein, joined with discernment, is the abiding threefold feeling, which they call pleasure, pain, and that which is neither pain nor pleasure.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaś ca mūrty atha ete hy āmaraṇāt pañca ṣaḍguṇā jñānasiddhaye
english: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, and then bodily shape—these five, six-qualitied, persist until death for the accomplishing of knowledge.

sanskrit: teṣu karmanisargaś ca sarvatattvārthaniścayaḥ tam āhuḥ paramaṃ śukraṃ buddhir ity avyayaṃ mahat
english: In them lies the issuing of action and the determining of the meaning of all truths; that they call the supreme radiance, the understanding, imperishable and great.

sanskrit: imaṃ guṇasamāhāram ātmabhāvena paśyataḥ asamyag darśanair duḥkham anantaṃ nopaśāmyati
english: For one who beholds this aggregate of qualities as though it were the self, the endless misery born of false views does not subside.

sanskrit: anātmeti ca yad dṛṣṭaṃ tenāhaṃ na mamety api vartate kim adhiṣṭhānā prasaktā duḥkhasaṃtatiḥ
english: And when it is seen as 'not the self,' then neither 'I' nor 'mine' holds sway: upon what foundation can the clinging stream of misery then rest?

sanskrit: tatra samyaṅ mano nāma tyāgaśāstram anuttamam śṛṇu yat tava mokṣāya bhāṣyamāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Here there is right-mindedness, the supreme teaching of renunciation: hear it, as it is spoken, for it shall be for your liberation.

sanskrit: tyāga eva hi sarveṣām uktānām api karmaṇām nityaṃ mithyāvinītānāṃ kleśo duḥkhāvaho mataḥ
english: For renunciation alone is the way; of all the works that are enjoined, when wrongly practiced, the constant toil is held to be but a bringer of pain.

sanskrit: dravyatyāge tu karmāṇi bhogatyāge vratāny api sukhatyāge tapoyogaḥ sarvatyāge samāpanā
english: In the renouncing of wealth lie ritual acts; in the renouncing of enjoyment, the vows; in the renouncing of pleasure, the discipline of austerity; but in the renouncing of all, fulfillment.

sanskrit: tasya mārgo 'yam advaidhaḥ sarvatyāgasya darśitaḥ viprahāṇāya duḥkhasya durgatir hy anyathā bhavet
english: This path of all-renunciation, free of duality, has been shown for the casting off of misery; otherwise an evil course would be the lot of man.

sanskrit: pañca jñānendriyāṇy uktvā manaḥṣaṣṭhāni cetasi manaḥṣaṣṭhāni vakṣyāmi pañca karmendriyāṇi tu
english: Having named the five organs of knowledge, with the mind as the sixth in consciousness, I shall now declare the five organs of action, the mind again being the sixth.

sanskrit: hastau karmendriyaṃ jñeyam atha pādau gatīndriyam prajanānandayoḥ śepho visarge pāyur indriyam
english: The two hands are to be known as the organ of action, the two feet as the organ of motion, the generative member for begetting and for pleasure, and the anus as the organ of excretion.

sanskrit: vāk tu śabdaviśeṣārthaṃ gatiṃ pañcānvitāṃ viduḥ evam ekādaśaitāni buddhyā tv avasṛjen manaḥ
english: And speech, for the sake of particular sounds, they know as the fifth, attended by the others; thus the mind, with the understanding, should set free these eleven.

sanskrit: karṇau śabdaś ca cittaṃ ca trayaḥ śravaṇasaṃgrahe tathā sparśe tathā rūpe tathaiva rasagandhayoḥ
english: The two ears, sound, and the mind—these three make up the grasping of what is heard; so too in touch, in form, and likewise in taste and smell.

sanskrit: evaṃ pañcatrikā hy ete guṇās tad upalabdhaye yena yas trividho bhāvaḥ paryāyāt samupasthitaḥ
english: Thus these qualities are five triads for the apprehending of their objects, whereby each threefold state arises in its turn.

sanskrit: sāttviko rājasaś caiva tāmasaś caiva te trayaḥ trividhā vedanā yeṣu prasūtā sarvasādhanā
english: The sāttvika, the rājasa, and the tāmasa—these are the three, in which the threefold feeling, with all its means, is brought forth.

sanskrit: praharṣaḥ prītir ānandaḥ sukhaṃ saṃśāntacittatā akutaś cit kutaś cid vā cittataḥ sāttviko guṇaḥ
english: Elation, fondness, joy, happiness, a wholly tranquil mind—arising from no cause or from some cause within the mind—this is the sāttvika quality.

sanskrit: atuṣṭiḥ paritāpaś ca śoko lobhas tathākṣamā liṅgāni rajasas tāni dṛśyante hetvahetutaḥ
english: Discontent, anguish, grief, greed, and impatience—these are the marks of rajas; they are seen to arise with cause or without.

sanskrit: avivekas tathā mohaḥ pramādaḥ svapnatandritā kathaṃ cid api vartante vividhās tāmasā guṇāḥ
english: Want of discrimination, delusion, heedlessness, sleep, and torpor—however they come to be, these are the manifold tāmasa qualities.

sanskrit: tatra yat prītisaṃyuktaṃ kāye manasi vā bhavet vartate sāttviko bhāva ity apekṣeta tat tathā
english: Therein, whatever arises in body or in mind joined with delight, one should regard as the working of the sāttvika state.

sanskrit: yat tu saṃtāpasaṃyuktam aprītikaram ātmanaḥ pravṛttaṃ raja ity eva tatas tad abhicintayet
english: But whatever is joined with affliction and unpleasing to the self, one should reflect that rajas has there come into play.

sanskrit: atha yan mohasaṃyuktaṃ kāye manasi vā bhavet apratarkyam avijñeyaṃ tamas tad upadhārayet
english: And whatever arises in body or mind joined with delusion, beyond reasoning and beyond knowing, that one should understand to be tamas.

sanskrit: tad dhi śrotrāśrayaṃ bhūtaṃ śabdaḥ śrotraṃ samāśritaḥ nobhayaṃ śabdavijñāne vijñānasyetarasya vā
english: For that being which rests upon the ear—sound abides in the ear; yet neither of the two suffices, by itself, for the cognition of sound, nor for any other cognition.

sanskrit: evaṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā nāsikā caiva pañcamī sparśe rūpe rase gandhe tāni ceto manaś ca tat
english: So too the skin, the two eyes, the tongue, and the nose as the fifth—in touch, form, taste, and smell—these, together with awareness and the mind.

sanskrit: svakarmayugapadbhāvo daśasv eteṣu tiṣṭhati cittam ekādaśaṃ viddhi buddhir dvādaśamī bhavet
english: The simultaneous functioning of their own activities resides in these ten; know awareness to be the eleventh, and understanding shall be the twelfth.

sanskrit: teṣām ayugapadbhāve ucchedo nāsti tāmasaḥ āsthito yugapadbhāve vyavahāraḥ sa laukikaḥ
english: When these do not function together, there is no tāmasic annihilation; but when they rest in simultaneous action, that is the ordinary commerce of the world.

sanskrit: indriyāṇy avasṛjyāpi dṛṣṭvā pūrvaṃ śrutāgamam cintayan nānuparyeti tribhir evānvito guṇaiḥ
english: Even having released the senses, having earlier seen what was heard from tradition, one who reflects does not roam astray, being attended by these three qualities alone.

sanskrit: yat tamopahataṃ cittam āśu saṃcāram adhruvam karoty uparamaṃ kāle tad āhus tāmasaṃ sukham
english: When the mind, stricken by darkness, swiftly makes an unsteady wandering and comes to rest in time, that they call the tāmasa pleasure.

sanskrit: yad yad āgamasaṃyuktaṃ na kṛtsnam upaśāmyati atha tatrāpy upādatte tamo vyaktam ivānṛtam
english: Whatever, joined to scriptural lore, does not wholly come to rest—there too it takes on darkness, manifest like untruth.

sanskrit: evam eṣa prasaṃkhyātaḥ svakarmapratyayī guṇaḥ kathaṃ cid vartate samyak keṣāṃ cid vā na vartate
english: Thus has this quality been enumerated, conditioned by its own activity; in some it functions rightly, in some it functions not at all.

sanskrit: evam āhuḥ samāhāraṃ kṣetram adhyātmacintakāḥ sthito manasi yo bhāvaḥ sa vai kṣetrajña ucyate
english: Thus the ponderers of the inner self call this aggregate the field; and the conscious state that abides in the mind is called the knower of the field.

sanskrit: evaṃ sati ka ucchedaḥ śāśvato vā kathaṃ bhavet svabhāvād vartamāneṣu sarvabhūteṣu hetutaḥ
english: This being so, what annihilation is there, or how should there be anything eternal, when all beings act from their own nature, each by its proper cause?

sanskrit: yathārṇavagatā nadyo vyaktīr jahati nāma ca na ca svatāṃ niyacchanti tādṛśaḥ sattvasaṃkṣayaḥ
english: As rivers that have entered the ocean abandon their distinct forms and their names, yet do not surrender their own substance—of such a kind is the dissolution of a being.

sanskrit: evaṃ sati kutaḥ saṃjñā pretyabhāve punar bhavet pratisaṃmiśrite jīve gṛhyamāṇe ca madhyataḥ
english: This being so, whence should consciousness arise again in the state after death, when the living self is wholly commingled and is grasped only midway?

sanskrit: imāṃ tu yo veda vimokṣabuddhim; ātmānam anvicchati cāpramattaḥ na lipyate karmaphalair aniṣṭaiḥ; patraṃ bisasyeva jalena siktam
english: But he who knows this insight of release, and unwearying seeks the self, is not stained by the unwished-for fruits of action, as a lotus-leaf is not by the water poured upon it.

sanskrit: dṛḍhaiś ca pāśair bahubhir vimuktaḥ; prajānimittair api daivataiś ca yadā hy asau sukhaduḥkhe jahāti; muktas tadāgryāṃ gatim ety aliṅgaḥ śrutipramāṇāgamamaṅgalaiś ca; śete jarāmṛtyubhayād atītaḥ
english: Freed from the many firm bonds—those of offspring and of the gods—when he abandons both pleasure and pain, then, liberated and without mark, he attains the highest course; and beyond the proofs of scripture, the lore of tradition, and its rites of blessing, he reposes, passed beyond the fear of old age and death.

sanskrit: kṣīṇe ca puṇye vigate ca pāpe; tatonimitte ca phale vinaṣṭe alepam ākāśam aliṅgam evam; āsthāya paśyanti mahad dhy asaktāḥ
english: When merit is spent and sin has departed, and the fruit that springs from these has perished, the unattached, taking their stand upon the stainless, markless ether, behold the great.

sanskrit: yathorṇanābhiḥ parivartamānas; tantukṣaye tiṣṭhati pātyamānaḥ tathā vimuktaḥ prajahāti duḥkhaṃ; vidhvaṃsate loṣṭa ivādrim arcchan
english: As the spider, turning round and round, abides though let fall when its thread is spent, so the liberated one casts off misery, which is shattered as a clod that strikes against a mountain.

sanskrit: yathā ruruḥ śṛṅgam atho purāṇaṃ; hitvā tvacaṃ vāpy urago yathāvat vihāya gacchaty anavekṣamāṇas; tathā vimukto vijahāti duḥkham
english: As the ruru deer leaves behind its old horn, or as the serpent in due course casts its skin, and goes without a backward glance, so the liberated one abandons misery.

sanskrit: drumaṃ yathā vāpy udake patantam; utsṛjya pakṣī prapataty asaktaḥ tathā hy asau sukhaduḥkhe vihāya; muktaḥ parārdhyāṃ gatim ety aliṅgaḥ
english: As a bird, forsaking a tree that is falling into the water, flies off unattached, so this one, abandoning pleasure and pain, liberated and without mark, attains the most exalted course.

sanskrit: api ca bhavati maithilena gītaṃ; nagaram upāhitam agninābhivīkṣya na khalu mama tuṣo 'pi dahyate 'tra; svayam idam āha kila sma bhūmipālaḥ
english: And there is too this verse sung by the king of Mithilā, who, beholding his city set ablaze with fire, said himself, so it is told—'Truly, not even a husk of mine is burning here.'

sanskrit: idam amṛtapadaṃ videharājaḥ; svayam iha pañcaśikhena bhāṣyamāṇaḥ nikhilam abhisamīkṣya niścitārthaṃ; paramasukhī vijahāra vītaśokaḥ
english: This station of immortality the king of Videha, having himself been here instructed by Pañcaśikha, surveyed in its entirety and with its meaning made certain; and supremely happy, freed of grief, he went his way.

sanskrit: imaṃ hi yaḥ paṭhati vimokṣaniścayaṃ; na hīyate satatam avekṣate tathā upadravān nānubhavaty aduḥkhitaḥ; pramucyate kapilam ivaitya maithilaḥ
english: For he who recites this teaching, sure of liberation, never falls away and ever beholds it thus; he does not suffer calamities, free of grief, and is released, as the king of Mithilā was upon coming to Kapila.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ kurvan sukham āpnoti kiṃ kurvan duḥkham āpnute kiṃ kurvan nirbhayo loke siddhaś carati bhārata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Doing what does a man attain happiness, doing what does he meet with misery, and doing what does he move through the world fearless and perfected, O descendant of Bharata?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca damam eva praśaṃsanti vṛddhāḥ śrutisamādhayaḥ sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: The elders, grounded in the sacred lore, praise self-restraint above all—self-restraint for every one of the social orders, and for the Brāhmaṇa most especially.

sanskrit: nādāntasya kriyāsiddhir yathāvad upalabhyate kriyā tapaś ca vedāś ca dame sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
english: For one who is not self-controlled, the due accomplishment of rites is not obtained; rite, austerity, and the Vedas—all rest upon self-restraint.

sanskrit: damas tejo vardhayati pavitraṃ dama ucyate vipāpmā nirbhayo dāntaḥ puruṣo vindate mahat
english: Self-restraint increases one's spiritual power; self-restraint is called the purifier; the self-restrained man, free of sin and fearless, attains the great.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ dāntaḥ prasvapiti sukhaṃ ca pratibudhyate sukhaṃ loke viparyeti manaś cāsya prasīdati
english: The self-restrained man sleeps in ease and awakens in ease; he moves through the world in ease, and his mind grows serene.

sanskrit: tejo damena dhriyate na tat tīkṣṇo 'dhigacchati amitrāṃś ca bahūn nityaṃ pṛthag ātmani paśyati
english: Spiritual power is upheld by self-restraint; the harsh man does not attain it, and forever he sees within himself a host of separate enemies.

sanskrit: kravyādbhya iva bhūtānām adāntebhyaḥ sadā bhayam teṣāṃ vipratiṣedhārthaṃ rājā sṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃbhuvā
english: As from beasts of prey, so from the unrestrained there is ever fear for living beings; for their restraint the king was created by the Self-Existent.

sanskrit: āśrameṣu ca sarveṣu dama eva viśiṣyate yac ca teṣu phalaṃ dharme bhūyo dānte tad ucyate
english: In all the stages of life self-restraint is held supreme; and whatever fruit there is in the duty of those stages, a greater is declared to lie in self-restraint.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ liṅgāni vakṣyāmi yeṣāṃ samudayo damaḥ akārpaṇyam asaṃrambhaḥ saṃtoṣaḥ śraddadhānatā
english: I shall tell the marks of those whose sum is self-restraint: absence of meanness, freedom from agitation, contentment, and a trusting heart;

sanskrit: akrodha ārjavaṃ nityaṃ nātivādo na mānitā gurupūjānasūyā ca dayā bhūteṣv apaiśunam
english: freedom from anger, constant uprightness, no overbearing speech, no conceit, honoring of elders, freedom from envy, compassion toward beings, and absence of slander;

sanskrit: janavādamṛṣāvādastutinindāvivarjanam sādhukāmaś cāspṛhayann āyāti pratyayaṃ nṛṣu
english: the shunning of gossip, of falsehood, of praise and of blame; desiring the good and coveting nothing, such a man wins the trust of men.

sanskrit: avairakṛt sūpacāraḥ samo nindāpraśaṃsayoḥ suvṛttaḥ śīlasaṃpannaḥ prasannātmātmavān budhaḥ prāpya loke ca satkāraṃ svargaṃ vai pretya gacchati
english: Stirring no enmity, of gracious conduct, equable in blame and praise, of good ways, endowed with character, serene in spirit, master of himself, and wise—he gains honor in the world and, after death, goes to heaven.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtahite yukto na smayād dveṣṭi vai janam mahāhrada ivākṣobhya prajñātṛptaḥ prasīdati
english: Devoted to the welfare of all beings, he hates no man out of pride; unshakable as a great deep lake, sated with wisdom, he abides serene.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyaḥ sarveṣām abhayaṃ yataḥ namasyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ dānto bhavati jñānavān
english: Since from him there is no fear to any being, and security to all, the self-restrained and wise man becomes one worthy of the homage of all creatures.

sanskrit: na hṛṣyati mahaty arthe vyasane ca na śocati sa vai parimitaprajñaḥ sa dānto dvija ucyate
english: He neither exults in great gain nor grieves in calamity; he, of measured wisdom, is called the self-restrained, O twice-born one.

sanskrit: karmabhiḥ śrutasaṃpannaḥ sadbhir ācaritaiḥ śubhaiḥ sadaiva damasaṃyuktas tasya bhuṅkte mahat phalam
english: Endowed with sacred learning and with good and auspicious deeds practiced by the virtuous, ever joined with self-restraint, such a man enjoys a great reward.
